;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Saudi Arabia–Yemen relations]], [[Yemeni Crisis (2011–present)]], [[Gulf of Oman incident]]
**Two [[Saudi Aramco]] oil pumping stations are attacked in an apparent drone strike according to [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabia's]] Energy Ministry. The stations are linked to a pipeline transporting oil from the eastern fields to the western coast port of [[Yanbu]] on the [[Red Sea]]. [https://www.apnews.com/c4da5c059fd841bf96d4103e55359329 (Associated Press)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-05-14/saudi-aramco-pumping-stations-targeted-in-limited-attack-spa (Bloomberg)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A 7.5 [[Moment magnitude scale|MMS]] quake rattles [[New Ireland (island)|New Ireland]], [[Papua New Guinea]]. Police Sergeant Frank Kilaur says that the quake was "very, very violent" but no immediate reports of major damages or casualties have been reported. A tsunami alert is issued by the [[Pacific Tsunami Warning Center]]. The tsunami threat has now largely passed. [https://ptwc.weather.gov/ptwc/text.php?id=pacific.TSUPAC.2019.05.14.1435 (Pacific Tsunami Warning Center)] [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/389216/7-point-5-quake-rattles-papua-new-guinea-s-rabaul (Radio New Zealand)] [https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/1127027/Papua-New-Guinea-earthquake-tsunami-solomon-islands-pacific (''Daily Express'')]

;International relations
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**[[United States Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] meets [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] and warns [[Russia]] to not interfere in the [[2020 United States presidential election]]. [https://www.npr.org/2019/05/14/723211912/on-visit-to-russia-pompeo-says-we-would-not-tolerate-interference-in-2020-electi (NPR)] [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/nation-world/article230372354.html (''Miami Herald'')]

;Law and crime
*Former [[New York City|New York]] [[New York's 9th congressional district|congressman]] [[Anthony Weiner]] is released from a [[halfway house]] in [[the Bronx]], completing his {{nowrap|21-month}} federal prison sentence for illicit online contact with a {{nowrap|15-year-old girl}}. [https://www.latimes.com/politics/la-na-pol-anthony-weiner-prison-sentence-released-20190514-story.html (''Los Angeles Times'')] [https://nypost.com/2019/05/14/anthony-weiner-released-from-bronx-halfway-house/ {{nowrap|(''New York Post'')}}]
*French [[Anesthesiology|anaesthesiologist]] Frédéric Péchier, previously investigated in the poisoning of seven patients at private clinics in [[Besançon]], France, is being held  over suspicions that he poisoned a further 17 - 50. Mr. Péchier has denied all charges, and is scheduled for a hearing later this week. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/french-anaesthesiologist-suspected-in-17-more-poisoning-cases-11541220 (CNA)]  [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48303733 (BBC News)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2019/05/14/french-anaesthologist-quizzed-suspected-poisoning-50-patients/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')]
*[[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections]]
**[[Governor of Florida|Florida Governor]] [[Ron DeSantis]] announces that [[Russia]]n hackers accessed voter databases in two Florida counties prior to the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 presidential election]]. No data or vote tallies were affected. [https://www.npr.org/2019/05/14/723215498/florida-governor-says-russian-hackers-breached-two-florida-counties-in-2016 (NPR)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**[[Venezuela]]n security forces surround the [[Palacio Federal Legislativo]] in [[Caracas]], preventing opposition [[National Assembly (Venezuela)|National Assembly]] lawmakers from entering the building to discuss a response to the recent arrest of National Assembly Vice President [[Edgar Zambrano]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2019/05/14/venezuela-security-forces-block-opposition-lawmakers-from-entering-parliament (Euronews)]

;Science and technology
*[[Microarchitectural Data Sampling]]
**[[Information security|Security researchers]] from [[Graz University of Technology]] and [[KU Leuven|Catholic University of Leuven]] discover a major new class of Microarchitectural Data Sampling [[Vulnerability (computing)|vulnerabilities]] called ZombieLoad in [[Intel]] [[Central processing unit|processors]], which, if exploited, can be used to steal sensitive information directly from the processor. Almost every computer with an Intel chip dating back to 2011 is affected by these vulnerabilities. [https://zombieloadattack.com/ (ZombieLoad disclosure website)] [https://techcrunch.com/2019/05/14/zombieload-flaw-intel-processors/ (TechCrunch)] 
**[[Linux kernel]] developers, [[Apple Inc.|Apple]], [[Google]] and [[Microsoft]] release emergency [[Patch (computing)|patches]] for their products to mitigate ZombieLoad. [https://techcrunch.com/2019/05/14/intel-chip-flaws-patches-released/ (TechCrunch)] [https://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=news_item&px=MDS-Kernel-Fixes (Phoronix)]
*[[Mass surveillance industry]]
**[[WhatsApp]] confirms a major security bug in the app let hackers remotely install surveillance software on its users' devices. All 1.5 billion users are urged to update WhatsApp as a precaution. The technology used in the [[cyberattack]] appears to have originated from [[NSO Group]], a technology company operating out of [[Israel]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-48262681 (BBC News)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/news/whatsapp-update-how-to-iphone-android-bug-hack-attack-security-a8912591.html (''The Independent'')]
